messages:
Nina (Support): FYI AuroraMed trial users can't finish onboarding their doc ingestion job errors out with `422` on indexing step. Lots of trial seats stuck. 
Raj (Support): Repro from their logs: POST /v1/docs -> 200 body accepted -> async index -> 422 {"error":"index schema mismatch"} request: req_a3d9c. Happened across three regions since 09:02 ET. 
Nina (Support): Customer flagged renewal check-in next Tue. They said expansion pilots hang if we don't unblock. Escalating to CS for comms + priority handling. 
Tara (CS): @Nina thanks. Can you confirm whether we received any malformed documents? Any PII concerns? Also need to know how many unique trial accounts impacted. 
Raj (Support): payload samples uploaded to ticket (https://app.redwood/tkt/8019). Rough count: ~24 trial users across 6 org users. Payloads look like nested JSON with unexpected nulls in `patient.addresses` array. No obvious PII exposure beyond what they'd expect. 
Tara (CS): Ok. Immediate ops plan: 1) Pause onboarding retries for affected orgs to avoid retry storm; 2) Offer manual CSV ingest route so they can continue trial while we fix index mapping; 3) Draft comms for renewal cadence: apologize, explain fix ETA, propose 1-week extension for pilot if needed. 
Ravi (Engineering): quick root cause note  Our index mapper rejects nulls in nested arrays since last deploy (schema tightening). We can relax validation and roll a patch within ~2 hours, or create a transformations pipeline to sanitize payloads which takes ~4-6 hours. 
Ben (AE): pinging Aurora contact Sara (cc'd) to confirm if they can provide sanitized sample or prefer us to transform. Also want to put them on a short status call. Sara is sensitive to data access so we should ask explicitly about consent for any temporary transform. 
Maya (CS Lead): +1 on consent ask. Also tag legal if we need to import their raw docs for transforms. If they ask for credits, route to me and Ben. Tara, please prep the customer note and I'll review before send. Keep tone proactive and offer concrete mitigations. 
ops-bot: Support ticket updated SUP-8019 priority: P1 (onboarding block) assigned to eng-ml. 
Nina (Support): Paused retries for orgs `aurora-trial-1..6`. Notifying customer that we're pausing automatic retries to avoid duplicate records. 
Raj (Support): Customer responded: "Please do the transform on your side, we can't re-export all our archived test data today." They explicitly declined sharing raw files externally. 
Tara (CS): Given decline, propose two paths in message: (A) we relax validation now (fastest, low risk) and patch index mapper; (B) we enable temporary CSV import UI they can upload sanitized exports (requires some enablement). Recommend (A) + offer (B) as follow-up. Also propose a pilot credit of 7 days and a dedicated enablement call within 24 hours. 
Ravi (Engineering): I can cut a relaxation patch to accept nulls in nested arrays and add safe-coercion in 90-120m. Will push a canary to staging, then to prod after smoke tests. Need support on test samples. 
Ben (AE): Noted. I'll schedule a 20-min sync with Sara for 11:30 ET and include our remediation plan. Tara, please include the credit offer in the message as optional and phrase it as "to make up for onboarding friction". 
Maya (CS Lead): Legal guidance: if we modify their data in-flight we need explicit written consent. But relaxing validation in our pipeline (no storage beyond processing) is low risk; still get an explicit yes. I'll loop Legal now. 
ops-bot: Legal pinged  LEGAL-3344 created. 
Tara (CS): Draft to Aurora (sample): "Hi Sara we're sorry for the friction. Root cause: our recent validation change rejects certain optional null fields in nested patient arrays. Plan: 1) We can roll a temporary safe validation relaxation in ~2 hours so your current trial flows resume. 2) If you prefer, we can enable a CSV upload for sanitized ingest. 3) As a gesture for the interruption we can offer a 7-day trial extension and a dedicated enablement session. Please reply with approval for (1) so we can proceed; if you consent, also confirm that temporary processing will not require us to persist any additional data beyond normal ingestion." Thoughts? 
Nina (Support): Customer replied: "Approve (1) — do it now. We don't want our trial paused." 
Ravi (Engineering): Pushing canary now. Will monitor index queue and report results in 15m. 
Raj (Support): ops note: watching for duplicate doc IDs — we set dedupe TTL to 12h to prevent re-index collisions. 
Ravi (Engineering): Canary results: 18/20 docs processed successfully; 2 failed with legacy enum values. Patch ready for prod push in 35m after final smoke. 
Tara (CS): Great. I'll send the customer note + schedule 30-min enablement for tomorrow to capture root cause, ask about automation for allowlisting fields, and gather feedback on our onboarding UX. Ben, loop me in on renewal messaging if they ask for extension beyond pilot credits. 
Maya (CS Lead): If they request formal credit beyond the 7 days, escalate to me and finance. Also record this incident as potential process change: include optional data-sanitization tips in onboarding docs. 
Nina (Support): Final update: prod patch deployed 11:45 ET, 26/26 queued trial docs processed. Closing P1 with note to re-open if further issues. 
Tara (CS): Closing summary for handoff doc: support escalation -> validation regression -> immediate retry pause -> customer-approved temporary validation relaxation -> prod patch in ~1h -> enablement + 7-day extension offered -> capture feedback and update onboarding docs. Will create a CS action item ticket for onboarding docs update. 
Maya (CS Lead): Thanks team. Tara, please get the handoff doc into the renewal playbook so AE has context for the upcoming renewal touch.
